newsitem.title: USA: HP cuts prices on PC's, memory kits.
newsitem.headline: HP cuts prices on PC's, memory kits.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co Monday said that it cuts prices on its HP Vectra XA and XU PC Workstations up to six percent and trimmed prices on its 32MB and 128MB memory kits.
In a statement, HP said the price cuts are effective immediately.

An HP Vectra XA PC with 200MHz Pentium Pro processor, 2.1GB Ultra SCSI hard drive, 32MB RAM and Matrox Millennium graphics card now is expected to sell for under $3,000. An HP Vectra XA PC with 166MHz Pentium processor with MMX technology, 2.5GB hard disk, 16MB RAM and CD-ROM drive, will cost $1,950, down five percent.

The list price of an HP Vectra XU PC Workstation has been reduced by up to 4.9 percent. An HP Vectra XU PC Workstation with 200MHz Pentium Pro processor, 4.5GB hard-disk drive, Matrox Millennium graphics card, 10/100Base-T PCI LAN card and CD-ROM drive is expected to sell for under $4,000.
The prices are for PCs without monitors.

HP also dropped prices on 32MB and 128MB ECC DIMM memory kits. The 32MB kit, with a list price cut of 12 percent, now is expected to sell for $300. The 128MB kit, with a list price cut of 28 percent, is expected to sell for $1,604.
